title: Implementation Details in Public Interface Documentation
pattern: Public doc-comments explaining private internal mechanics — fields, helper types, data structures, algorithms, or loop structures — instead of the interface contract.
why_bad: Leaky abstraction. Callers of public APIs should not be exposed to internal implementation choices; this couples callers and documentation to volatile internals and increases maintenance on every refactor.
detection: Doc-comments (`///`) on public items referencing private fields, private helper types, inner loops, algorithm names, or threading primitives of the implementation.
counterexample: A public doc-comment describing only externally observable behavior (e.g., 'Creates a connection pool with the specified capacity limit'), with mechanism notes kept as `//` comments inside the body.
fix: Move implementation details to internal inline comments (`//`) inside the function body; keep the doc-comment focused strictly on the API contract.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 13.2 ("Red Flag: Implementation Documentation Contaminates Interface").
